{{short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}}{{use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Makati''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Makati]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Makati's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Makati's 2nd congressional district|second]] districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Rizal|Legislative districts of Manila}} [[File:Makati legislative district map (2023).svg|thumb|250px|Makati legislative district map
{{color box|#8fce00}} 1st district
{{color box|#0057c7}} 2nd district under the jurisdiction of Makati following the [[Makati–Taguig boundary dispute]]
{{color box|#46aaff}} Former barangays of the 2nd district now under the jurisdiction of [[Taguig]] following the Makati–Taguig boundary dispute]] Areas now under the jurisdiction of Makati were initially represented as part of the [[Manila's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the [[Manila (province)|province of Manila]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] from 1898 to 1899. The then-town was later incorporated to the province of [[Rizal (province)|Rizal]], established in 1901, and was represented as part of the [[Rizal's 1st congressional district|first district]] of Rizal from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. Then excluding the areas of present-day [[Embo, Taguig|Embo barangays]],{{cite map |author = |title = Map of the City of Manila |trans-title = |map = |map-url = |date = |year = 1942 |url =https://assets.isu.pub/document-structure/210327135441-504a42fce9e9c0dafe948e678988e3b0/v1/68eac8a829832842ad677a95008f9037.jpg |scale = 1:40,000 |series = |publisher = Division of Drafting and Surveys, Office of the City Engineer and Architect, City of Manila |cartography = |page = |pages = |section = |sections = |inset = |edition = |location = |language = |format = |isbn = |id = |access-date =August 29, 2022 |archive-url = |archive-date =}} Makati was incorporated to the [[City of Greater Manila]] during [[World War II]] and was represented as part of the at-large district of Manila from 1943 to 1944. Areas now under the jurisdiction of the aforementioned barangays, meanwhile, was part of the at-large district of Rizal during the war-time legislature. Makati was separated from Rizal on November 7, 1975 by virtue of Presidential Decree No. 824,{{cite PH act|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/presdecs/pd1975/pd_824_1975.html|chamber=PD|number=824|date=November 7, 1975|access-date=October 10, 2017|title=Creating the Metropolitan Manila and the Metropolitan Manila Commission and for Other Purposes}} and was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] along with other [[Metro Manila|Metropolitan Manila]] municipalities and cities as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV]] from 1978 to 1984. Makati first gained separate representation in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative]] to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]]. The municipality continued to constitute a separate [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional district]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=October 9, 2017}} proclaimed on February 11, 1987; it elected its member to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine House of Representatives elections|that same year]]. Upon its cityhood, Makati was divided into two congressional districts by virtue of Section 52 of Republic Act No. 7854 (the City Charter of Makati),{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=7854|url=https://thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-7854.php|title=An Act Converting the Municipality of Makati into a Highly Urbanized City to be Known as the City of Makati |date=July 19, 1994 |access-date=August 29, 2022}} enacted on January 2, 1995 and approved by plebiscite on February 4, 1995, the day Makati became a city. The districts first elected their separate representatives in the [[1995 Philippine general election|1995 general elections]]. However, 2nd district representative-elect [[Agapito Aquino]] was disqualified before he could assume office due to lack of residency. Aquino's disqualification was later criticized for failing to consider the legal impossibility of meeting the one-year residency requirement in newly created districts that had existed for less than a year.{{cite PH act|chamber=GR|number=120265|date=September 18, 1995|accessdate=August 13, 2025|url=https://lawphil.net/judjuris/juri1995/sep1995/gr_120265_1995.html|title=Aquino vs. Commission on Elections}} As a result, [[Joker Arroyo]], elected from the 1st district, sat as the only representative of the city for the [[10th Congress of the Philippines|10th Congress]]. Makati only began having two seated representatives following the [[1998 Philippine general election|1998 elections]]. {{further|Makati–Taguig boundary dispute}} There was a dispute over which city has jurisdiction over lands encompassed within the former Fort McKinley U.S. Military Reservation (now [[Fort Bonifacio]] and its surrounding areas). Portions of two of [[Makati]]'s barangays ([[Post Proper Northside, Makati|Post Proper Northside]] and [[Post Proper Southside, Makati|Post Proper Southside]]) were claimed by the neighboring city of [[Taguig]] as part of its own four barangays ([[Fort Bonifacio (barangay)|Fort Bonifacio]], [[Pinagsama]], [[Western Bicutan]], and Ususan). Residents of areas where Makati exercised ''de facto'' control vote as part of the [[Makati's 2nd congressional district|2nd congressional district]], while residents of areas where Taguig exercised ''de facto'' control vote as part of its [[Taguig–Pateros's 1st congressional district|first congressional district]] for Ususan and its [[Taguig–Pateros's 2nd congressional district|second congressional district]] for Fort Bonifacio, Pinagsama, and Western Bicutan. In April 2023, the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]] has decided to junk Makati's petition to overrule its earlier decision to side with Taguig in the case of the [[Embo (barangays)|Embo]] barangays, effectively placing these barangays into the jurisdiction of Taguig.{{cite news|url=https://mb.com.ph/2023/4/3/taguig-lgu-lauds-sc-decision-over-fort-bonifacio-ownership|title=Taguig LGU lauds SC decision over Fort Bonifacio ownership|first=Jonathan|last=Hicap|date=April 3, 2023|work=Manila Bulletin}}{{cite news|url=https://www.philstar.com/nation/2023/04/05/2256966/makati-raises-constitutional-issues-bgc-land-dispute|title=Makati raises 'constitutional' issues in BGC land dispute|first=Marc Jayson|last=Cayabyab|date=April 5, 2023|accessdate=April 6, 2023|work=The Philippine Star}} The [[Department of the Interior and Local Government]] released a memorandum circular dated October 26, 2023 transferring the control of the ten Embo barangays, including [[Post Proper Northside]] and [[Post Proper Southside]], to Taguig.{{cite news |last=Caliwan |first=Christopher Lloyd |date=November 8, 2023 |title=DILG's Taguig office to take control of 10 EMBO villages |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1213248 |work=Philippine News Agency |access-date=November 13, 2023}} With this, the fate of Makati's 2nd district is uncertain as its remaining barangays of Guadalupe Nuevo, Guadalupe Viejo, and Pinagkaisahan do not fulfill altogether the constitutional requirement of 250,000 residents. Makati could be reduced back to a single district with [[Legislative districts of Pateros–Taguig|Taguig–Pateros]] gaining a district,{{cite news |last1=Aurelio |first1=Julie |title=SC ruling opens issue on Taguig House seats |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1805272/sc-ruling-opens-issue-on-taguig-house-seats |access-date=23 July 2023 |work=Philippine Daily Inquirer |date=22 July 2023 |language=en}} but pending legislation, the status quo of its existence is expected to prevail.{{cite news |title=After SC ruling, Makati's congressional seat hangs in the balance |url=https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/in-depth/after-supreme-court-ruling-land-dispute-makati-congressional-seat-hangs-balance/ |access-date=27 July 2023 |work=Rappler |date=26 July 2023}} On September 27, 2024, the Embo barangays were finally reapportioned between Taguig–Pateros's two existing districts.{{cite news|url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/elections/comelec-allows-embo-residents-taguig-vote-congressman-2025/|title=Comelec allows EMBO residents in Taguig to vote for congressman in 2025|date=September 27, 2024|accessdate=September 28, 2024|work=Rappler|first=Dwight|last=de Leon}} == Historical and defunct district boundaries == {| class="wikitable" |- !colspan="9" | District boundary changes |- !Year !Map !District constituencies
